thread:
incbot: ALERT: dedicated-pool 'aurum-enterprise' GPU utilization > 98% for 6m (queue depth 72) — paging oncall
oncall_ryan: I'm on it, pulling metrics now. paging SRE
sre_maya: joining. seeing 4 nodes at 100% GPU, 2 nodes spiking OOM-ish logs. queue is mostly infer requests from aurum-prod (single enterprise tenant).
oncall_ryan: timeline? when did it start?
sre_maya: surge started ~6832109500, steady increase. tail latency > 1200ms P95, error rate from runtime 5% (kv-cache evictions).
eng_runtime_lead: fwiw model variant is rdx-13b-qa-1 (fp16 q8). serialization + kv cache pressure likely. Can we spill to a fallback model?
account_exec_zoe: customer-facing here — Aurum Ops (cust_ops_ivan) is on a call. need ETA and if we'll be doing a burst.
cust_ops_ivan: Confirmed incident on our side, customers seeing timeouts. We have a handful of high-traffic jobs running right now — can you give an interim mitigation?
sre_maya: Options: 1) immediate burst from spare dedicated buffer (needs AE approval, may hit billing/limits). 2) autoscale additional nodes (takes ~4-6m to provision in this VPC). 3) degrade to smaller model for non-critical requests (requires routing change).
infra_tom: cloud pool has 2 hot spare GPUs in the same AZ; policy permits temporary burst up to 2 nodes for enterprise if account exec approves. provisioning path is fast but needs infra runbook step.
oncall_ryan: Zoe — can you authorize burst? it's the quickest fix.
account_exec_zoe: I can approve a 2-node burst for 30m. Notify customer and billing. :white_check_mark:
cust_ops_ivan: Appreciate it. we'll throttle non-essential jobs on our end as well.
eng_runtime_lead: On my side I'll prepare a routing rule to strip large-batched requests > 64 tokens and route them to fallback rdx-6b for a few minutes. snippet: ```route override: if request.batch_size>64 -> model=rdx-6b-fallback```
sre_maya: Starting burst now — invoking infra runbook step 3. provisioning request submitted.
incbot: ACTION: runbook#dedicated-burst invoked by oncall_ryan at 6832110100
infra_tom: new nodes provisioning, ETA ~3m.
eng_runtime_lead: Applying routing rule now. blocking large-batch traffic to 6b fallback.
(2m pass)
infra_tom: hot-spare nodes attached to aurum-enterprise pool. GPU utilization back down to 65% cluster-wide. queue depth -> 12.
sre_maya: latency P95 back to ~220ms, error rate down to 0.5%. good so far.
cust_ops_ivan: Confirmed lower error rate on our side, thanks. still seeing occasional spikes but acceptable.
oncall_ryan: leaving the burst active for 20m while we monitor. please don't escalate to eviction.
account_exec_zoe: Billing notified, temp-boost flagged to customer account, invoice override possible if needed.
product_lee: flagging for post-incident review: why did kv-cache evict so aggressively? add to RCA.
eng_runtime_lead: action: add cache size telemetry to per-tenant dashboard, and consider conservative cache eviction thresholds for single-tenant pools.
sre_maya: scheduling 30m follow-up call in 1h to decide permanent mitigation (autoscale policy tweak vs reserved capacity increase).
oncall_ryan: handing off to night oncall in 25m — @sre_maya will continue monitoring.
sre_maya: noted. I'll watch the pool and will escalate if utilization > 85% again.
cust_ops_ivan: Thanks team. We'll report if customer traffic reduces further. Appreciate quick response. :heart:
incbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: burst active until 6832111900 (expires automatically) — monitor metrics dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dash/aurum-enterprise
(30m later)
sre_maya: burst expired, nodes detached, cluster back to normal steady-state. no regressions in next 30m. closing incident after postmortem.
account_exec_zoe: sending follow-up note to Aurum Ops with summary and ask about traffic pattern changes.
product_lee: RCA item created: "tenant cache thrash on sustained high-batch workloads". assigned to eng_runtime_lead.
eng_runtime_lead: will prototype conservative per-tenant cache policy + fallback routing automation.
sre_maya: incident closed for now. follow-up meeting invite sent.
oncall_ryan: good job everyone.
